full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 228

Zhang v. Li and Liu — dispute over custody rights

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on May 30, 2024)

Keywords

Civil; custody rights; minor; during marriage; equal custody rights

Ruling Gist

1. Where, during the period of separation between spouses, one spouse or his or her close relatives takes away the minor child without authorization, causing the other spouse to be unable to meet with the minor child, this constitutes an infringement of the rights arising from the other spouse's performance of parental duties.

2. In a dispute over custody rights during the period of spousal separation, a people's court may, by reference to the provisions of the Civil Code concerning child support after divorce, tentatively determine the arrangements for the care of the minor child and specify that the party temporarily having direct care of the minor child has the obligation to assist the other party in performing parental duties.

Basic Facts

Zhang (female) and Li registered their marriage in May 2019 and subsequently lived together in a community in Baoding City, Hebei Province. They had a daughter, Li (the minor child), in November 2020. From April 19, 2021, Zhang and Li began living separately and later failed to reach an agreement on divorce. On July 7, 2021, Li (the father) and Liu (the paternal grandmother) took Li (the minor child) away without the permission of Zhang (the mother) and brought her to a village in Dingzhou City, Hebei Province. At that time, Li (the minor child) was still in the breastfeeding period. Zhang repeatedly requested to visit the child but was refused by Li. Zhang then filed a divorce lawsuit, and the court, on January 13, 2022, rendered a judgment dismissing the divorce petition. Although the marital relationship continued, the spouses were effectively separated, during which Li (the minor child) lived with Li and Liu, and Zhang was unable to visit the child for an extended period. On January 5, 2022, Zhang filed a lawsuit on the ground of a dispute over custody rights, requesting the court to order Li and Liu to return Li (the minor child) and to allow Zhang to continue exercising her custody rights over Li (the minor child) in accordance with the law.

Judgment

The Dingzhou City People's Court of Hebei Province rendered a civil judgment on March 22, 2022, dismissing the plaintiff's claims. After the judgment was pronounced, Zhang appealed, and the Baoding Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province rendered a civil judgment on July 13, 2022: 1. Reversing the civil judgment of the first instance by the Dingzhou City People's Court of Hebei Province; 2. Li (the minor child) was to be temporarily directly cared for by the appellant Zhang; 3. The appellee Li was permitted to visit Li (the minor child), and the appellant Zhang was obligated to assist and cooperate with the appellee Li in visiting Li (the minor child).

Reasoning

The disputed issues in this case are: whether the unauthorized taking of Li (the minor child) by Li (the father) and Liu (the paternal grandmother) constituted a tort, and how to properly address the issues of the care and custody of Li (the minor child) when the spouses, though still in a marital relationship, were effectively separated.

First, regarding whether the unauthorized taking of Li (the minor child) by Li (the father) and Liu (the paternal grandmother) constituted an infringement on Zhang (the mother). Article 34, paragraph 2, of the Civil Code provides: "Rights arising from a guardian's performance of guardianship duties in accordance with the law shall be protected by law." Article 1058 provides: "Both spouses have equal rights to raise, educate, and protect their minor children and share the obligation to raise, educate, and protect their minor children." Both parents are the guardians of their minor children and equally enjoy the rights to raise, educate, and protect them. In this case, Li and Liu took away Li (the minor child), who was still in the breastfeeding period, without authorization and refused to return her to Zhang, resulting in Zhang's prolonged inability to visit the child and causing Li (the minor child) to be weaned prematurely and deprived of her mother's care. The conduct of Li and Liu not only harmed the physical and mental health of the minor child but also constituted an infringement on the rights arising from Zhang's performance of parental duties. The first-instance court's dismissal of the claims on the ground that Zhang had no evidence that Li had failed to properly care for Li (the minor child) was an erroneous application of the law.

Second, regarding how to address the issue of the care and custody of Li (the minor child) during the period of spousal separation. In this case, from birth until she was taken away by Li (the father) and Liu (the paternal grandmother), Li (the minor child) had been breastfed by her mother Zhang and, as of the time the lawsuit was filed, was less than two years old, making her a very young minor. Although both parents have equal custody rights over the child, the exercise of such rights must comply with the principle of the best interests of the ward. While the current laws and judicial interpretations do not contain specific provisions on the exercise of custody rights during marriage, taking into account that both parties were in a state of separation prone to heightened conflict, and in order to maximize the protection of the minor child's interests, the court, by reference to the principle established in Article 1084 of the Civil Code that "after divorce, a child under two years of age shall be directly cared for by the mother as a rule," determined that it is appropriate for Li (the minor child) to be temporarily directly cared for by Zhang. During the period when Zhang directly cares for Li (the minor child), she shall assist and cooperate with Li in visiting Li (the minor child).

Relevant Legal Provisions

Articles 34, 1058, 1084, and 1086 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

Articles 4 and 24 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors
